# RGEEtools

RGEEtools provides helpers for defining a region of interest, sampling HYCOM
ocean datasets hosted on Google Earth Engine, and converting sampled features
to an R data frame.

## Requirements

The sampling functions require an initialized Google Earth Engine account and
the [`rgee`](https://r-spatial.github.io/rgee/) package. Install and configure
`rgee` following its setup instructions, then initialize Earth Engine in your
own R session. Loading RGEEtools does not initialize Earth Engine or attach
other packages.

```r
install.packages("rgee")
rgee::ee_Initialize()
```

## Installation

```r
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("JaceInnis/RGEEtools")
```

## Example

The example below samples HYCOM velocity for a polygon and converts the
returned feature collection into a data frame. It requires a working Earth
Engine configuration and an internet connection.

```{r example, eval=FALSE}
library(RGEEtools)

region <- ROI(
  "[-99, 31], [-99, 18], [-80, 18], [-80, 31]"
)

velocity <- wvtolist(
  ROI = region,
  date = "20180805",
  interval = 5,
  scale = 30000,
  depth = 0
)

velocity_data <- geetodf(velocity)
head(velocity_data)
```

The `date` argument is the exclusive end of the averaging window, following
Earth Engine's `filterDate()` convention. The requested HYCOM bands and
sampling region/resolution must be available within the upstream dataset and
Earth Engine's request limits.

Use `?ROI`, `?wvtolist`, `?wttolist`, `?wstolist`, `?ssetolist`,
`?geetodf`, and `?thin` for argument details and examples.
